decks.notes: This deck focuses on utilizing hatebear creatures to disrupt the opponent's strategy while pushing an aggressive game plan. By combining cards like Anointed Peacekeeper, Archon of Emeria, and Chancellor of the Annex with powerful mana acceleration from cards like Ancient Tomb and Moxen, the deck aims to lock down opposing spells while beating down the opponent with efficiently costed threats. Using cards like Cavern of Souls to protect its creatures and disruptive cards like Chalice of the Void and Wasteland to control the board, the deck looks to create a strong advantage and close out the game quickly.

The deck focuses on utilizing disruptive spells and mana denial strategies to control the opponent's resources and limit their options. By leveraging counterspells like Force of Will and Spell Pierce, along with removal spells like Swords to Plowshares, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while setting up its own win conditions. Lavinia, Azorius Renegade and Orcish Bowmasters provide additional disruption, while cards like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time help maintain card advantage. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value and resilience in longer games.

This deck focuses on utilizing the Doomsday combo to quickly win the game by manipulating the top of the library and casting Thassa's Oracle to win the game on the spot. The deck includes key cards like Force of Will for protection, Dark Ritual for fast mana acceleration, and various tutors to find the necessary combo pieces. The goal is to assemble the combo and win the game before the opponent has a chance to respond, making it a high-risk, high-reward strategy in Vintage 1 vs 1 gameplay.

The deck focuses on quickly generating mana and card advantage through the use of artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen, along with powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Paradoxical Outcome. The goal is to assemble a combo involving cards like Time Vault and Voltaic Key to take multiple turns in a row, while using disruptive spells like Force of Will to protect the combo. Lurrus of the Dream-Den provides additional value by allowing you to recast key cards from the graveyard.

The deck focuses on assembling a powerful combo involving Coveted Jewel, which can generate massive mana advantage and card advantage. The key cards in the combo are Paradoxical Outcome and Phyrexian Metamorph, which can be used to generate infinite mana and draw the entire deck. Additionally, Time Vault and Voltaic Key provide an alternative win condition. The deck is designed to quickly assemble the combo pieces while controlling the game with disruptive spells like Force of Will and Sink into Stupor. The goal is to overwhelm the opponent with a powerful, game-ending combo.

The main goal of this deck is to quickly fill your graveyard with powerful creatures like Golgari Grave-Troll and Ichorid using cards like Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder. Once these creatures are in the graveyard, you can use cards like Narcomoeba and Prized Amalgam to quickly bring them onto the battlefield. Additionally, using cards like Grief and Creeping Chill can disrupt your opponent's game plan while also providing you with additional advantages. The deck aims to overwhelm your opponent with a combination of speed and powerful creatures, ultimately leading to a victorious outcome.

This deck focuses on using control elements to disrupt the opponent's game plan, while maintaining card advantage through powerful draw spells and interaction. The goal is to eventually outvalue the opponent by efficiently answering threats and generating incremental advantage over time. The deck utilizes a variety of disruption spells, counterspells, and removal alongside card advantage engines like Dig Through Time and Treasure Cruise. Lurrus of the Dream-Den provides additional value by allowing the player to recur low-cost permanents from the graveyard. Overall, the deck aims to grind out incremental advantages and close out the game with powerful threats or by depleting the opponent's resources.

The deck focuses on creating disruption and slowing down the opponent's game plan while maintaining pressure with aggressive creatures. By utilizing hatebears like Anointed Peacekeeper, Archon of Emeria, and Chancellor of the Annex, the deck aims to control the board and limit the opponent's options. With the support of mana acceleration from cards like Chrome Mox and Ancient Tomb, the deck can quickly deploy threats and disrupt the opponent's strategy. March of Otherworldly Light provides additional removal options, while Cavern of Souls ensures that key creatures cannot be countered. This deck excels at disrupting the opponent's plans while applying pressure on multiple fronts.

This deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy while maintaining card advantage through efficient card draw and using key spells like Force of Will and Fatal Push to control the board. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds extra value by allowing you to recur low-cost permanents. By controlling the tempo of the game and disrupting the opponent's plays, this Dimir Control deck aims to outlast and outplay its opponents until it can secure a win through careful resource management and strategic decision-making.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan with hate cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, while also applying pressure with aggressive creatures like Anointed Peacekeeper and Stillmoon Cavalier. It utilizes mana acceleration from cards like Chrome Mox and Ancient Tomb to quickly establish a board presence. The deck also aims to disrupt the opponent's mana base with cards like Wasteland and Strip Mine, while protecting its own creatures with Cavern of Souls and Karakas. Overall, the deck aims to control the game while applying consistent pressure on the opponent.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent and limiting their options while applying pressure through aggressive creatures. It utilizes cards like Archon of Emeria, Chancellor of the Annex, and Witch Enchanter to hinder the opponent's spells and resources. Additionally, the deck includes hate cards like Chalice of the Void and Anointed Peacekeeper to further impede the opponent's game plan. With efficient mana acceleration from cards like Chrome Mox and the Moxen, the deck aims to quickly establish a board presence and keep the opponent on the back foot.

The focus of this deck is to assemble the combo of Doomsday and Thassa's Oracle to win the game. The deck is built around powerful card draw and filtering spells like Ponder, Brainstorm, and Preordain, along with fast mana sources like Black Lotus and Dark Ritual. The goal is to use Doomsday to set up a winning pile of cards, then use Thassa's Oracle to win the game immediately. The deck also includes disruption like Force of Will and Flusterstorm to protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's game plan.

The deck focuses on controlling the game through disruption, card advantage, and countering key spells. It utilizes cards like Force of Will, Force of Negation, and Spell Pierce to counter opposing threats while using cards like Ancestral Recall, Dig Through Time, and Treasure Cruise to draw cards and find answers. By controlling the board with removal like Swords to Plowshares and countering spells, the deck aims to outvalue the opponent and secure victory through card advantage and efficient plays.

The deck is focused on disrupting the opponent's game plan with cards like Collector Ouphe and Force of Will, while also applying pressure with creatures like Leovold, Emissary of Trest and Oko, Thief of Crowns. It has a mix of removal spells like Abrupt Decay and Fatal Push to deal with threats, along with disruptive spells like Mental Misstep and Daze. The deck's aim is to control the board and limit the opponent's resources while gradually building up its own board presence to secure a quick victory.

The deck focuses on quickly filling the graveyard with cards like Stinkweed Imp and Golgari Thug to bring back powerful creatures like Ichorid and Prized Amalgam. Using cards like Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder to quickly cycle through the deck, the goal is to utilize the Dredge mechanic to create a strong board presence and overwhelm the opponent. The deck also includes disruption in the form of Force of Will and Grief to protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's game plan.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 deck focuses on aggressive creatures with disruptive abilities to slow down and control the opponent's game plan. The Hatebears archetype aims to limit the opponent's resources and options while maintaining a steady stream of threats to apply pressure. By using creatures like Anointed Peacekeeper, Archon of Emeria, and Chancellor of the Annex, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy while still dealing damage and advancing its own game plan. The deck also utilizes mana acceleration and disruptive artifacts to further impede the opponent's progress.
